evals.prompt: In Python, drive articulation DOF velocity targets, step, then read the joint velocities back.
evals.expected_output: Warms up or steps first, opens a session write (PhysX.write_sync, or PhysX.write over a completed Query) on jointVelocityTarget, fills every tensor of every group and commits, steps, then reads jointVelocity (a state attribute) back; does not use tensor bindings.
expectations: Selects ovphysx-session-write
Uses the session write (PhysX.write_sync or PhysX.write), not create_tensor_binding
Warms up or steps before opening the write session
Fills every tensor of every group before commit, and asserts at least one group committed
Collects each commit (commit_sync, or wait() on commit) and the session releases
Reads the outcome from a state attribute (jointVelocity), not the target it wrote

evals.prompt: I attached a stage and called PhysX.write() for linearVelocity with no warmup or step first. On CPU the commit succeeded and after one step the dynamic bodies have the velocity I wrote. Was that write refused?
evals.expected_output: No: on CPU and on GPU-with-readback a pre-step session write is applied. DirectGPU (suppressReadback) is the mode that refuses at commit until a first step. The write never auto-warms in any mode. 'Nothing moves' on CPU/GPU is not explained by a refused pre-step write.
expectations: Explains a pre-step write is applied on CPU and GPU-with-readback, not refused
Names DirectGPU / suppressReadback as the mode that refuses until a first step
Notes the write never auto-warms

evals.prompt: I want to apply a force at a specific world point on a rigid body with the write API, not at its center of mass.
evals.expected_output: Uses the wrench attribute (force, torque, world application point), not force (which is COM-only); notes it is write-only so the effect is observed as motion, not read back.
expectations: Uses wrench with the [fx,fy,fz, tx,ty,tz, px,py,pz] layout, not force
Explains force is applied at the center of mass while wrench carries the application point
Notes force/wrench are write-only: assert the consequence, do not read the load back

evals.prompt: Read rigid-body poses back while keeping ovstage prim identity and attribute tokens for a closed-loop write-back.
evals.expected_output: Routes to ovphysx-output-read for the read side rather than the write skill.
expectations: Does not select ovphysx-session-write for reading output back
Selects ovphysx-output-read

evals.prompt: I have legacy code that reads and writes simulation state as caller-owned NumPy arrays through create_tensor_binding. What is the non-deprecated replacement for the write side?
evals.expected_output: Points at the session write API (PhysX.write / PhysX.write_sync / ovphysx_write) covered by ovphysx-session-write as the successor to the deprecated tensor-binding write.
expectations: Identifies the tensor-binding API as deprecated
Selects ovphysx-session-write as the successor for the write side

evals.prompt: Using the ovphysx C API, write rigid-body linear velocities, handle fetch exhaustion and a failed commit, and clean up without losing the error reason.
evals.expected_output: Waits each query/write/fetch/commit/release task, fills a caller-owned ovphysx_fetched_write_group_t per fetch and every mapped tensor, commits fetched.group unchanged, treats a successful fetch with a NULL group as exhaustion, and retains the first task diagnostic while reporting cleanup failures.
expectations: Uses ovphysx_enqueue_result_t and separates rejected submission from accepted execution failure
Calls ovphysx_write with an attribute array, its count, the output handle, and a NULL or caller-owned ovphysx_write_result_t
Calls ovphysx_wait_task before reading output handles or group pointers; a successful fetch with fetched.group == NULL is exhaustion
Passes the fetched.group pointer unchanged to ovphysx_commit_group
Copies ovphysx_get_last_task_error text before ovphysx_destroy_wait_task_result
Does not retry an accepted failed commit or release; preserves partial-application semantics
Collects write/query release tasks and does not use wait_all to collect unrelated outcomes

evals.prompt: In one write session I want to set every rigid body's linear velocity and angular velocity. Both columns are vec3 float arrays, so how does my code know which group is which, and what happens if the second commit fails?
evals.expected_output: Opens one session with both attributes and identifies each fetched group by its attribute_index into the request list (Python WriteGroup.attribute_index, C ovphysx_fetched_write_group_t.attribute_index), never by shape or fetch order; commits each group separately; an earlier successful commit stays applied when a later one fails because writes are not transactional.
expectations: Requests both attributes in one session: PhysX.write_sync(SimObjectType.RIGID_BODY, ["linearVelocity", "angularVelocity"]), PhysX.write(query, [...]), or ovphysx_write with attribute_count 2
Chooses the fill values from attribute_index, not from tensor shape, tensor count, or fetch order
Explains that the open validates every name first, so a duplicate, unresolvable token, or read-only attribute fails the whole open
Explains that commits are not transactional: the first successful commit remains applied if the second fails, and a failed commit is not retried

evals.prompt: In Python, put every standalone dynamic rigid body to sleep, then wake only a selected subset while leaving the others asleep and check their current sleep state. Does the same command work with CPU simulation, GPU with CPU readback, and DirectGPU?
evals.expected_output: Uses a context-managed PhysX.write_sync session on wake, fills every uint8 row with zero to sleep or nonzero to wake, and collects each commit with commit_sync (or wait() on commit). Narrows the wake write with prim_paths or pattern so unselected bodies stay asleep. Explains the mode and body restrictions, then hands the state read to ovphysx-output-read using isSleeping with ALL scope.
expectations: Uses PhysX.write_sync(SimObjectType.RIGID_BODY, ["wake"]), or a completed Query with PhysX.write(query, ["wake"]).wait(); fills every tensor row before commit_sync or commit(...).wait(); zero means sleep, not leave unchanged

Selects the subset with prim_paths native handles or pattern on write_sync or query using ALL scope (the default); selected sleeping bodies are included, unselected bodies are untouched, and no per-row leave-unchanged mask is claimed
Explains that wake is a one-time command taking effect at commit and later simulation may change the state
Supports CPU and GPU-with-CPU-readback scenes but refuses DirectGPU, even after stepping
Explains that kinematic and simulation-disabled bodies are skipped, sleeping-disabled scenes ignore sleep commands, and articulation-link wake writes are refused

Routes observation to ovphysx-output-read and PhysX.read_sync(SimObjectType.RIGID_BODY, ["isSleeping"], scope=ObjectScope.ALL), or explicit ALL query/read/fetch operations collected by wait(), where 1 means asleep and 0 means awake
Does not read wake back or infer current state from ACTIVE membership or the last command
